findings_and_reconciliations.trace: For terrain-kind scenarios the parent first applies phase_validation_frames, slicing after the first phase wrap. P17 ScenarioHeightMetrics then applies the same helper again for contact-to-passing height, visual peaks, and phase-height range, on the already filtered frames. Current metrics does the same. When the filtered slice contains another phase wrap, the second call drops all remaining frames through that wrap; a complete first post-calibration cycle in that slice cannot contribute to these three height measures. The adjacent peak-loop comment says every complete post-warmup cycle is independently gated, subject to the explicitly excluded trailing partial cycle.

Whether the first post-calibration cycle must count and whether any independent gates reject such a run remain owner/policy questions. No execution, supported phase sequence, rejected/accepted report or runtime impact shown.

findings_and_reconciliations.trace: Both P17 and current make liveness required only if the first metadata identifies a repeatable procedural raised-guard scenario and every supplied frame exceeds the stationary speed limit. P17 returns NotApplicable otherwise; current returns default required=false, which current gate exempts. A single stationary or slow frame thus affects the whole liveness cohort, but the source alone does not show that any supported intended steady scenario may legitimately produce such a frame. For a required half step, P17 requires swing-foot bone and clearance in every frame; current requires endpoints but filters missing interior clearance before the max. Missing interior samples alone cannot prove a false liveness success or absent terrain policy failure.
